questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to get to your destination quicker.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of tiredness while driving. You are too tired to drive safely if you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or turn up the radio to stay awake. If you notice these signs, park in a safe place and rest.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Tight enough to silence the seat belt alarm.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights in fog, snow, or heavy rain?
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, and heavy rain. High beam light reflects off these conditions and causes glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing the street illegally, not at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: You do not have to stop for them.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally or jaywalking. Always stop for pedestrians.

questions.question: What happens to fines for moving traffic violations in school zones?
questions.explanation: In Maine, fines for moving traffic violations are doubled in school zones. Drive carefully when passing through school zones.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Adjust your speed as needed to turn safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you become tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. Regulation signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns you to be ready for traffic merging from the right side.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area marked for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are often marked with white lines to show where pedestrians can cross. Some crosswalks have extra lines between or instead of the parallel lines. Some crosswalks have no markings at all.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning signals, should you slow down, look, and listen?
questions.explanation: If a railroad crossing has no warning devices or only a crossbuck sign, slow down. Look both ways on the tracks and listen for a train. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: Do safety belts help you stay alert by keeping you from slouching while you drive?
questions.explanation: Safety belts keep you from slouching and help you stay alert. They also reduce fatigue by keeping your body in place as the car moves and turns.

questions.question: When can you drive in a lane with a red X signal above it?

options.text: When there is no oncoming traffic.
When you are passing another car.

questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. A red X means the lane is closed. Never drive in a lane with a red X.

questions.question: When can you park directly across from a fire station entrance?

options.text: If the emergency vehicles just left

questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire station driveway entrance or directly across from it. This rule is in most local laws.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow other cars instead of the flagger.
Assume the flagger should not be there.

questions.explanation: Follow all directions from flaggers in construction zones. Slow down and be careful when told to do so. Not following these directions is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, what should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes you to make poor decisions about speed and distance. It increases crash risk. When tired, you could fall asleep while driving and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows brain activity and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows reaction time and impairs judgment.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner, ready to cross in front of you. What should you do before turning right?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver as they pass.
Speed up as they pass you.

questions.explanation: Get out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact. Speeding up or blocking them will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: You miss your exit on an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Exit at the next exit and return to the missed exit.
Ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and return to the missed exit.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on a highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: In a car with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to sit?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags can be dangerous for children. Anyone age 12 or under should sit in the back seat.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are near.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that bicycles may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving to avoid staring at one thing too long.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and keep drivers safe. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: While backing out of your driveway.

questions.explanation: Adjust all mirrors before starting your engine so you can see without leaning forward or backward. You won't have time to adjust them while driving in traffic.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, what should you do?

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving before you drive.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving before you drive.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. Always talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine will affect you before you drive.
